item.title: NYC's New Mayor Says He Found A $12 Billion Deficit When He Took Office, Double What The Previous Administration Admitted
item.description: https://www.reddit.com/r/BoredPandaHQ/s/7QwraTj1aV https://www.factcheckradar.com/fact-check/mamdani-erases-12-billion-deficit-in-first-budget According to official statements from the NYC Mayor's Office and reporting from multiple news outlets, Mayor Zohran Mamdani inherited a budget deficit exceeding $12 billion. During his budget presentation on May 12, 2026, the Mayor confirmed that this gap had been reduced in stages, first to $5.4 billion and finally to zero. This fiscal turnaround was made possible by a significant partnership with Governor Kathy Hochul, who secured nearly $8 billion in state assistance over two years to stabilize the city's finances. The balanced budget relies on several new fiscal strategies, including a projected $500 million annually from a new pied-à-terre tax on non-resident second homes valued over $5 million, as well as $1.47 billion in agency savings. However, the methods used to reach this zero-dollar balance have drawn sharp criticism. Reports indicate that a significant portion of the 'state aid' involves 'kick-the-can' measures, such as restructuring $2.2 billion in pension plan payments and delaying mandates for school class sizes. Critics, including the Citizens Budget Commission, have labeled these as 'pension gimmicks' and 'temporary plugs' that may exacerbate future fiscal problems. While the current deficit has been eliminated on paper for the upcoming fiscal year, city Comptroller Mark Levine warned that the reliance on one-shot measures could lead to a $7 billion shortfall by 2028. Political opponents have also characterized the initial deficit warnings as 'tactical chess' or 'performative' theater designed to pressure the state for funding. Despite these long-term concerns and political debates over the methods, the immediate claim regarding the elimination of the inherited $12 billion deficit is accurate based on the executive budget release. Source quality: The report is based on an official press release from the NYC Mayor's Office and corroborating reports from multiple reputable news outlets, including CBS New York, amNewYork, and the New York Post, all dated May 12, 2026. These sources provide both the official figures and critical analysis of the budget's sustainability.

item.description: Air Force crews flew every American bomber out of England on Sunday, some before the tankers meant to refuel them on the way home were in the air. Commanders ordered them back from RAF Fairford after new warnings of an Iran-backed plot against the base, a week after British police arrested five men nearby. For the first time in months, the base that launched bombing runs on Iran this year has no American bombers. America and Israel attacked Iran on February 28 in a war Donald Trump said would take four weeks or less. Seven months later, he says America will win it "right after the election." American service members and thousands of Iranians have already died, and the crews who fly those bombers couldn't wait for November. item.title: I Cut a Natural Green Gem That Glows Blue in Daylight
item.description:
This is the latest gem I finished cutting. It is a special fluorite that came from the famous Rogerley Mine in the UK, known for its rich green crystals and remarkable blue daylight fluorescence. Rogerley has now closed, but the nearby Diana Maria Mine in Frosterley, Weardale, County Durham, England, continues to produce extraordinary material. Its many pockets have yielded fluorite with unique colors and impressive daylight fluorescence. What drew me to this particular crystal was the combination of deep green color, strong daylight fluorescence, and the clarity needed to cut a beautiful gemstone. Fluorite isn’t something we typically cut, but this piece was worth the challenge. It’s a collector’s gemstone, though. Fluorite is soft and easily damaged, making it impractical for wear. While you occasionally see it in jewelry, I strongly recommend keeping this one as a gem to collect, admire, and share with friends. Getting a good polish required some adjustments. We’ve had trouble polishing fluorite on our harder laps in the past, so I ordered a special, softer lap for this stone. But the biggest challenge was preserving its daylight fluorescence. In this particular crystal, the strong blue daylight response was concentrated in a thin layer near the natural crystal surfaces rather than evenly throughout the material. That meant I needed to follow those natural faces and remove as little material as possible from the pavilion (the underside of the gem). Cut too far, and I could still have a beautiful green stone, but lose the blue fluorescence that made it so special. That’s why the pavilion has an unusual design. It’s just one main facet and a culet facet. I paired that simple pavilion with a step-cut crown, carefully working around what the crystal would allow. The result exceeded my expectations. Despite the minimal faceting on the pavilion, the brilliance is surprisingly beautiful and, most importantly, I preserved that incredible blue daylight fluorescence. To appreciate it best, view it in diffused daylight rather than direct sunlight. The ultraviolet component of daylight brings out the blue fluorescence, and stronger UV generally produces a stronger response. Under a longwave UV lamp, it fluoresces intensely, too. (As seen below) My favorite part is showing someone what happens when we move it from indoor lighting into daylight. A rich green gemstone suddenly takes on an extraordinary blue glow right before their eyes. That reaction never gets old. For someone who collects unusual gems, loves fluorescent minerals, or wants a gemstone with a memorable party trick, this is a special piece. This fluorite will be available during our next live streaming gem show on our YouTube channel here: YouTube.com/MoreGems — You can also visit MoreGems.com to explore many other beautiful gemstones we’ve cut. -Steve Moriarty
Here we show the natural crystal before it was cut. It shows it as the green color you’ll see in normal indoor lighting, the the daylight fluorescent blue when we walk it outside. Super cool fluorescent response, which is rare in the gem and mineral world!
Another view under a long wave uv flashlight showing the strong blue fluorescent response for this material!
This shows the deep green fluorite in normal indoor lighting, then the response under a long wave UV flashlight. The fluorescence is amazing!
Color Under normal lighting conditions.
Color under a fluorescent light source.
I know many of you are going to like it better natural, so I thought I would share a couple of natural specimens that won’t be cut. These are a couple examples of the new material currently coming from the Diana Maria mine. This particular specimen is a very aesthetically pleasing piece with the deeply colored fluorite on top of a bed of quartz. It is from the Milky Way Pocket.
It has a very strong daylight fluorescent response. More details on these specimens can be found on www.MineralMike.com
Here is another relatively newer specimen from the Diana Maria mine. This piece has a similar rich green color and deep blue daylight fluorescent response like you saw with the Rogerly material. This pieces is from the Greedy Hog Pocket, discovered in 2023.
It has a good daylight fluorescent response. More details on these specimens can be found on www.MineralMike.com
Here is the finished gem once again. You can see the deep blue fluorescent response due to the uv from the sunlight. Such a spectacular color! If you have any questions about this fluorite, lapidary, or anything else gem related, please let me know!

item.title: “...we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” - Sam Altman
item.description: "By Christine Mui and Brendan Bordelon 10/04/2026 04:55 PM EDT OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said there remains a fundamental difference in worldview between his company and rival Anthropic on artificial intelligence regulation, arguing in an exclusive interview with Decoded by POLITICO that the technology’s benefits justify accepting some risks — and that AI should remain broadly accessible to the public. “I think there’s a lot of daylight,” Altman told Decoded co-author and POLITICO senior tech reporter Brendan Bordelon. Asked specifically where he diverges from Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei, Altman said, “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” Anthropic has long been viewed as the strongest proponent of AI regulations within the industry, a stance that until recently was at odds with the lighter-touch approach favored by OpenAI. But the policy differences between the two leading AI firms have narrowed in recent months, with OpenAI backing tougher rules as it grapples with high-profile hacking incidents and rogue behavior by its models. Altman agreed with Amodei’s call last month to slow the development of the most advanced AI models. His company has followed Anthropic in endorsing new state laws that impose stricter safety requirements than what the maker of ChatGPT had previously supported — a subtle shift from its prior state strategy. And OpenAI lobbyists recently endorsed a bipartisan House proposal that would require top AI companies to embed outside safety evaluators." from https://www.politico.com/news/2026/10/04/sam-altman-decoded-interview-ai-01106217
